heading: Public Tac output and private Yon lifetime
body: The build checks the tac member of client/manifest.json. It publishes the manifest at /manifest.webmanifest for web bundles and staged native bundles. A browser also finds it there to install the app. The manifest can have other members beside tac, and it still binds without changes. Only the tac member is configuration. The build never opens .env, never resolves production secrets and never publishes yon. Browser services load this public JSON through an injected HTTPClient. They bind it themselves with Setting. Native services still load it themselves with their SDK, and they own it. The browser HTTPClient transport is network-only (no-store) unless a read is marked Cached. It is not an offline cache loader. A change to client/manifest.json causes a development reload for Tac. A change to Yon settings or .env secrets needs a server restart. The deployment controls runtime executables, isolation policy, environment allowlists and capabilities. They are not options in the application files. YON_APPLICATION_JSON is reserved output of the supervisor. An operator cannot use it as an override.
